description: We are a team of students passionate about science, technology, and solving real-world problems. We aim to use NASA’s data and resources to develop a creative solution for this year’s Space Apps Challenge. We are looking for motivated teammates interested in coding, science, engineering, data analysis, design, or research. Most importantly, we value creativity, teamwork, initiative, and a willingness to learn.
summary:
ECHOES is an interactive space exploration platform that brings the science, engineering and forgotten stories of NASA missions to life through three complementary 3D experiences.

The Curiosity Discovery Explorer introduces visitors to the instruments and systems used to investigate Mars through interactive hotspots, educational storytelling and guided missions.

The Mars Driving Simulator allows users to operate a simulated rover, navigate Martian terrain, control scientific equipment and experience an automated investigation sequence.

The Apollo 11 Eagle Explorer recreates key stages of a historic lunar mission, allowing users to investigate the Lunar Module, follow landing and ascent operations, and discover why its descent stage remained on the Moon.

Inspired by NASA's Abandoned but Not Forgotten challenge, ECHOES combines storytelling and hands-on simulations to explain the engineering behind space exploration and the legacy of equipment left behind.

Built with web-based 3D technologies and supported by NASA educational resources, the project aims to inspire curiosity, scientific thinking and STEM learning.
details:
ECHOES — Every Mission Leaves a Story Behind

ECHOES is an interactive, browser-based educational experience developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, inspired by the challenge Abandoned but Not Forgotten: Storytelling about NASA's Discarded Equipment on the Moon and Mars.

Every successful space mission depends on remarkable engineering. Yet while we celebrate the spacecraft that continue exploring, we often overlook the equipment that made their journeys possible. When NASA's Curiosity rover landed on Mars in 2012, its heat shield, backshell, parachute and descent stage were left behind. These objects remain evidence of the ingenuity and engineering decisions behind the mission.

ECHOES explores how interactive storytelling can make these overlooked contributions more accessible, particularly to younger audiences. Our current prototype introduces visitors to Curiosity and the scientific systems that its landing equipment helped deliver safely to Mars.

How the experience works

Visitors begin by selecting one of two exploration modes:

  • Free Exploration: Explore a detailed 3D model of Curiosity, rotate the camera, zoom in on components and select interactive hotspots to discover how different instruments operate.
  • Guided Mission: Follow a structured investigation called A Mystery on Mars, with instructions, highlighted instruments, educational stories and navigation between discoveries.

The interactive rover features seven discoveries: Mastcam, ChemCam, the Robotic Arm and Drill, SAM, CheMin, Wheels and the MMRTG power system.

Each discovery introduces a scientific or engineering function through approachable storytelling, smooth camera transitions and additional explanations. The experience encourages visitors to investigate questions such as how scientists study Martian rocks, identify minerals and understand ancient environmental conditions.

Technology and development

ECHOES was developed using React, TypeScript, Vite, Three.js, React Three Fiber, Drei, Tailwind CSS and React Router. It uses a NASA/JPL-Caltech Curiosity 3D model and supporting NASA scientific documentation. The illustrative Martian landscape incorporates a third-party 3D terrain model credited to its original creator.

The website is hosted on Vercel, with source code managed through GitHub. Its responsive interface supports desktop and mobile exploration, including touch controls, keyboard interaction and reduced-motion preferences.

Creativity and impact

Rather than presenting space science as a collection of technical facts, ECHOES presents scientific instruments as a team of detectives, each with a unique ability to uncover clues about Mars.

This approach combines immersive 3D visualization, interactive investigation and narrative learning to make complex engineering and planetary science more approachable.

Our intended impact is to inspire curiosity about science, technology, engineering and mathematics (STEM), encourage independent exploration and help audiences appreciate the less-visible technologies that make space missions successful.

Throughout development, we considered scientific accuracy, accessible language, mobile usability, visual engagement, performance, source attribution and the distinction between documented NASA discoveries and fictional storytelling elements.

Our longer-term vision is to expand ECHOES into interactive stories devoted directly to equipment left behind on the Moon and Mars, preserving the engineering history of missions long after individual components have completed their roles.
